mainEntity.name: Can I change the content myself after handover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. That is what the content model and handover document are for: every section you are expected to update is listed with exactly where to change it.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the code and domain?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. The source code, domain and hosting account are handed over in your name.

mainEntity.name: Do you redesign our current site or start from scratch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Either. In Discover we check which parts of the current site are worth keeping and write the result into the scope.

mainEntity.name: Which content management system do you use?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on who changes content and how often. The choice and the reason go into the scope.

Website building
A website with structure: modeled, built, and handed over with documentation, so it keeps working after launch day.
Problem

items: A site built without structure or documentation looks complete on launch day and becomes hard to maintain afterwards. You do not know where to change content, every small edit depends on the person who built it, and the page that matters for sales loads slowly.

blocks.html: Who it is for

items: Founders building their first serious site who want to update content themselves later.
Teams whose current site is slow, or that nobody but the previous builder can change.
Businesses that need a bilingual Persian and English site where both versions actually work.

blocks.html: Who it is not for

items: If a ready-made template in your colours is enough; a site builder does that for less.
If you need to be online within days and there is no time to define a scope.
If you want building to start before any content exists, with content arriving "later", without accepting that risk in the scope.

blocks.html: Approach

items: Discover. Input: a conversation with you and any existing content. Output: brief and draft scope. Owner: dadmor, with your answers.
Model. Input: the brief. Output: site map and content model (which sections each page has, and who updates them). Owner: dadmor; approval: you.
Design. Input: approved site map. Output: design system and key pages. Owner: dadmor; feedback: you.
Build. Input: approved design and final content. Output: a working site on a staging environment and a draft handover document. Owner: dadmor.
Launch and handover. Input: approved site. Output: live site, handover walkthrough, final handover document. Owner: dadmor; domain and hosting access: you.

blocks.html: Deliverables
Scope and timeline factors

items: What moves the work from S to M to L: number of pages, features (forms, search, multiple languages), integrations (payment, booking, a content management system), and content readiness.
Bilingual means two sets of content and an RTL and LTR check on every page; we scope it separately.
What you supply: text and image content, logo and brand identity, domain and hosting access, and one named decision-maker for approvals.
What usually delays projects: content that is not ready (first), feedback that arrives late, and access that cannot be found on launch day.

blocks.html: Effort band

items: Band S, M or L, using the estimator's rule table. We give a fixed price after the scoping conversation, in a written proposal.

blocks.html: A band is the rough size of the work, not a price and not a duration. A fixed price is set only after a scoping conversation, in a written proposal.
The band is a starting estimate; the scoping conversation may move it.
Limits and risks

items: We do not promise a specific Google ranking. We deliver structure, speed and technical readiness for search.
Writing the content is not part of this service unless it is in the scope; see Marketing and content for that.
Domain, hosting and third-party service costs are yours, and the accounts stay in your name.
Third-party services (payment gateways, booking) can change after launch; support after the handover period is by written agreement only.
We work as one studio and take a limited number of projects at once; the start date depends on capacity at that time.
